tweet.text:
Mutation testing is cpu intensive.  Claude wrote a nice little tool that does it.  It first runs coverage and then mutates every covered operator and runs the appropriate test suite between each mutation.  Any mutant that survives is evaluated.  Some equivalence cases that no test can kill.  The others are killed by writing the tests that cover those paths.  

This grows the test suite and covers virtually every path through the code.  That's an impressive constraint for the AI to try to cheat it's way out of.
